attempts.raw_response: Upon returning to Belgrade, he worked as a writer and translator, contributing to various literary magazines. His experiences living abroad deeply influenced his fiction, which often explores themes of displacement, memory, and cultural identity. Stanković’s time in London and later travels to Lisbon and Cairo provided rich material for his narratives, blending personal history with the landscapes of these cities. His novel *Zamalek* was particularly praised for its vivid portrayal of expatriate life in Egypt, while *Estoril* delved into the complexities of post-war Europe. Stanković continues to write and is a prominent voice in contemporary Serbian literature, frequently participating in international literary festivals and workshops.

pair.human_continuation:
Subsequently, Stanković relocated to Lisbon, Portugal. There he pioneered translating literary works from Serbian language to Portuguese and vice versa. Among others, Stanković translated the works of Jose Saramago, Ivo Andrić and Dragoslav Mihailović.

His first book, Odakle sam bila, više nisam i druge lisabonske priče, was published under Geopoetika in 2011. It was followed by the critically acclaimed Estoril in 2015. The book was nominated several international awards, including the Serbian NIN Award and the International Dublin Literary Award. His final work, Zamlek, published through Laguna in 2021, was introduced to the school book report in Portugal.

In 2017, Tiago-Stanković signed the Declaration on the Common Language of the Croats, Serbs, Bosniaks and Montenegrins.

In the evening of 20 December 2022, Stanković died at his home in Lisbon at the age of 57.

Tiago Stanković published three books in Serbian: Odakle sam bila, više nisam i druge lisabonske priče (2011), Zamalek (2015) and Estoril (2020), which were also translated to English, Portuguese and Macedonian. He was recognized as one of most read Serbian contemporary authors.

Biography 
Stanković was born in Belgrade, SR Serbia, SFR Yugoslavia on 2 November 1965. After graduating with a degree in architecture, he moved to London, England, where he lived until 1995.
